d2_answers.question: Separate organic growth from acquisition/consolidation effects.
d2_answers.fact: 2026H1 revenue was RMB328.46m, up 15.30% versus the restated 2025H1 base of RMB284.88m; net profit was RMB130.98m, up 35.32% versus the restated base. The unadjusted 2025H1 revenue and net profit were only RMB212.68m and RMB84.99m. Historical comparatives were restated for the same-control acquisition of the Hulunbuir extreme-testing center. Parent-company revenue rose from RMB206.93m to RMB273.31m.
d2_answers.interpretation: The restatement removes a large portion of the acquisition-accounting distortion: apparent revenue growth versus the originally reported 2025H1 would have been about 54%, but the comparable group growth rate is 15.3%. Parent-company revenue growth of roughly 32% confirms meaningful growth in the pre-existing corporate perimeter, but the disclosure still does not provide a clean same-site bridge separating Salt City ramp, pricing/mix and other organic effects.
d2_answers.judgment: PARTIAL_IMPROVED. Organic growth is now better evidenced, but exact same-site organic growth remains unreconstructable.

d2_answers.question: Model utilization, pricing, incremental margins and ROIC for new testing capacity.
d2_answers.fact: The 2026H1 report discloses Salt City project-level realized benefit for the first time in the D2 record: RMB23.1461m in 2026H1 and RMB30.1414m cumulative, against RMB1,295.815m cumulative actual investment and stated expected benefit of RMB188.470m. The company explicitly marks the project as not reaching expected benefit because capacity remains in ramp. A prior primary IR disclosure stated 2025 Salt City Phase II revenue of about RMB68m and profit before tax of about RMB16m, while management could not commit to a timetable for 70%-80% utilization.
d2_answers.interpretation: The prior evidence gap has narrowed from 'no realized project economics' to 'early realized economics available but not mature enough for underwriting'. The H1 benefit/investment relationship is still far below the 8%-10% mature after-tax research hurdle on a simple capital-efficiency screen, but ramp timing, benefit-definition differences and incomplete utilization/price data prevent a clean project ROIC calculation. The ice/snow base remains in construction with zero realized benefit and expected full operation in 2028.
d2_answers.judgment: HOLD_EVIDENCE_GAP_NARROWED_NOT_CLEARED. Do not mark D2 complete until utilization, pricing/mix and a fuller annualized benefit/return series permit mature ROIC reconstruction.

d2_answers.question: Assess convertible-bond dilution and balance-sheet implications.
d2_answers.fact: The RMB1.03904bn convertible bond was completed with RMB1.03048bn net proceeds and RMB5.99 initial conversion price. At 2026-06-30 the H1 disclosure showed most newly raised proceeds had not yet translated into operating benefit; the ice/snow project remained under construction and disclosed zero realized benefit.
d2_answers.interpretation: Liquidity and funding runway are strong, but capital deployment risk remains material. Dilution risk is not offset by demonstrated earnings accretion yet, so financing completion alone does not improve the research disposition.
d2_answers.judgment: COMPLETE_NO_UPGRADE. Funding risk is lower; capital-efficiency and potential dilution risks remain active.

d2_answers.question: Map competitive moat and customer concentration.
d2_answers.fact: The H1 report describes a nationwide multi-climate testing network spanning Salt City, Hulunbuir, Hainan, Changchun and Ningbo-related capacity, with more than 200 customers and leading share in selected heavy-commercial-vehicle and intelligent-connected testing niches. It also explicitly warns that OEM self-built proving grounds, third-party operators and newly opened capacity are increasing supply and price competition. The last complete concentration evidence remains 2025 top-five customers at 57.25% of revenue and controlling shareholder CATARC-related demand at 20.17%.
d2_answers.interpretation: Physical/scenario coverage, regulatory/testing know-how and the CATARC ecosystem remain real advantages, but they are not monopoly-like: customer concentration and expanding industry capacity mean the moat must be validated through third-party demand, pricing resilience and utilization rather than asset breadth alone.

d2_answers.question: Define valuation ceiling and utilization/ROIC kill conditions.
d2_answers.assumption: Retain the R1 analytical ceiling framework of about 30x normalized RMB220-250m earnings, roughly RMB5.0-5.7/share before full-conversion dilution, until mature project returns are demonstrated. Do not raise the ceiling because H1 earnings growth accelerated while Salt City remains below expected project benefit.
d2_answers.judgment: HOLD. Kill conditions remain: Salt City stays materially below expected benefit after another full operating year; mature after-tax return on major new capacity fails the 8%-10% research hurdle; third-party demand/pricing weakens while customer concentration rises; or convertible-bond dilution occurs without proportionate earnings accretion. The 2026H1 evidence increases concern on the first condition but is not yet a formal kill because management still identifies the project as ramping.

evidence_gap.missing: Mature project-level utilization, realized pricing/mix, incremental margin and a sufficiently long realized benefit/return series to calculate normalized after-tax ROIC for Salt City; the ice/snow base remains pre-operation.
